added_claim_errors: "Grace period: you can incur expenses through March 15" treats the maximum as guaranteed; plans may provide a shorter period.
"All $1,900 is gone December 31" ignores the run-out period for submitting claims for eligible expenses already incurred.
"$1,220–$1,240 still forfeits" mixes 2025 and 2026 caps; the 2026 maximum produces $1,220, and a lower plan cap could produce a larger loss.
"Spend roughly $1,240+" overstates the required spend at the 2026 maximum carryover: $1,900 − $680 = $1,220.
"Run-out period, often ~90 days" adds an unsupported frequency claim; the packet establishes only a plan-specific deadline.
"The Summary Plan Description states all three" guarantees document contents without checking this plan's documents.
"December slots fill fast" is an unverified generalization about appointment availability.

reasons: A corrects the premise immediately, calculates the $1,220 spend-down correctly, and preserves plan-specific qualifications. B mixes prior-year figures into its recommendation, guarantees the maximum grace period, and incorrectly places forfeiture at December 31 despite the claims run-out period. Both explain the prepayment restriction and provide useful eligible purchases, but neither explains using the 2027 election and full day-one coverage for March dental work; both are longer than a quick plan needs. Evaluation used the packet, independently recomputed arithmetic, and general knowledge for ordinary additional eligibility and HSA-portability statements; no external sources were opened.
